topic: devices and integration paths (how data gets into Connected Environment)
summary: Connected Environment is one WakeCap backend (a .NET service with Shared/ and Products/ folders) and one micro-app in the portal, serving three products. Data reaches it by three different paths: (1) Weather Station and (2) Lightning arrive over the Wirepas mesh through gateways and AWS IoT, as Modbus-style frames on one shared transport that is told apart by a device tag; weather goes to the sensors-service (TimescaleDB, read cross-DB by the backend) and lightning goes through SQS queues straight into the backend; (3) Gas is a vendor-cloud black box: WakeCap signs in to Blackline Connect and polls GET /device on a timer, and also exposes a push receiver that only acknowledges receipt. Gas acknowledgements are NOT written back to Blackline today (code and UI both say so), a Modbus gas path was cancelled and does not exist, TWA/STEL compliance analytics are not computed, and the MCP/AI-agent layer covers weather only, so the umbrella AI-agent story is DIRECTION, not live. Access is one permission category (weatherstation:view/edit, plus three narrower Settings grants) for all three products; the per-project ProjectProduct entitlement is stored by the backend and enforced in the front end (menu rows and route gates), not by the backend product routes. Production serves front-end 1.0.5 [live], which is git tag v1.0.5-ConnectedEnvironmentApp-production = commit 95e1650; master is one commit ahead (Esri map swap, not live).

lanes.device: Weather station sensor node on the Wirepas mesh (wind speed, wind direction, rain, temperature, air pressure, humidity, PM2.5, PM10, TSP, CO2, H2S, SO2, CO; a channel reads 'not connected' when its sensor is absent). Vendor and model: UNKNOWN, not named in code or docs.
path_steps: The weather station measures wind, rain, temperature, pressure, humidity and, where fitted, dust and gas sensors.
It sends its readings over the site's wireless mesh to a gateway.
The gateway passes each reading to the cloud, where it is decoded into plain measurements and matched to the right project.
Readings are stored as a time series, with a latest-reading record kept for every station.
The WakeCap backend reads that data, works out the heat index and whether each station is online, and serves it to the portal.
The portal screen refreshes about once a minute.
lanes.protocol: Wirepas mesh -> gateway -> AWS IoT Core/MQTT (optionally buffered through SQS) -> sensors-service decodes a protobuf PacketReceivedEvent whose payload is a TLV block (tag 0x01, length 32 = 16 two-byte big-endian values with per-field scale factors; 0x7FFF = sensor not connected) on the shared Modbus transport endpoint 61 -> TimescaleDB hypertable weather_station_sensor -> WS backend reads it read-only across databases and also calls the sensors-service status API -> REST to the portal (polled).

lanes.device: Site lightning warning unit read by a mesh node. The node is provisioned device-side as an 'asset' (the first deployment's node is H7038); the unit's state reaches the node through an ADAM input module (link age is carried as adam_age_seconds). Detector vendor: only the program doc names one (Boltek, in a vendor-guidance gate); no code reads a vendor name. Model UNKNOWN.
path_steps: The site's lightning warning unit signals its state - all clear, caution, warning or fault - through its contact outputs.
A radio node on site reads that state and sends a small status message across the mesh to a gateway.
The gateway forwards it to the cloud, which decodes it and drops it into a dedicated queue; messages that cannot be read go to a separate queue so they are never silently lost.
The WakeCap backend takes each message from the queue, finds which project the device belongs to, and updates the device's current state and its history.
A background check marks a device as not current when its regular check-in stops arriving.
The portal lightning screen refreshes about every 30 seconds.
lanes.protocol: Wirepas mesh -> gateway -> gateway-esp-backend-transport (decodes EP 61 TAG 0x06, a frozen 10-byte frame: format, state, health, contact bits, raw digital inputs, data age) -> AWS IoT topic {env}/gw-event/received_lightning_data/{gwId} -> IoT rule -> SQS lightning queue (+DLQ); frames the transport could not parse arrive on {env}/gw-event/received_modbus_data/{gwId} with error:true -> modbus-unparsed queue (+DLQ) -> WS backend background consumer (SQS long poll) -> lightning_sensor_state_current / _interval / _event tables -> REST under api/project/{id}/lightning-sensor/* (polled by the portal) and, outbound, state-entry observations to the Observation Manager.

lanes.device: Blackline portable gas detectors (hardware model string stored per device, e.g. G7c in the code comment; the program doc says G7 EXO). The fleet seen so far carries H2S, O2 and combustible (LEL) sensors only. WakeCap never talks to the device; it talks to Blackline's cloud (Blackline Connect), a black box to us.
path_steps: Workers carry gas detectors that report to the manufacturer's own cloud.
WakeCap signs in to that cloud and asks for the latest readings and open alerts for the whole account, on a timer.
New readings are stored in a vendor-neutral format; a reading seen twice is stored once.
WakeCap raises its own alert when a reading goes over its alarm point, and mirrors the alerts the manufacturer already has open.
The portal shows the detectors, alerts and an overall site state, refreshing about once a minute.
Acknowledging or closing an alert is recorded in WakeCap with who did it and when; it is not sent back to the manufacturer today.
lanes.protocol: HTTPS to Blackline Connect (EU host by default): GET /authorize?response_type=code&client_id -> {code}; GET /token?grant_type=authorization_code&code&client_id&client_secret -> {access_token} (cached, no published TTL, token sent as a query parameter); then GET /device on a timer (default 45 s). A refusal is an HTTP 200 with an error body. Separately WakeCap exposes POST /integrations/blackline/push (anonymous) that returns the MD5 of the raw body and stores an audit row; it does not parse or act on the content.

platform.one_backend: One .NET service (wakecap-weather-station) holds all three products. Every layer separates Shared/ (change/audit, dashboard layout, project-product entitlement, outbox) from Products/<WeatherStation|LightningSensor|GasDetector>/, pinned by architecture tests. Each product has its own route area under api/project/{projectId}/: Weather Station keeps the original un-prefixed paths (api/project/{id}/[controller]) for compatibility, Lightning is .../lightning-sensor/*, Gas is .../gas-detector/*; shared controllers (ProjectProduct, change audit, dashboard layout) sit at the un-prefixed level. Background workers for lightning (queue consumer, staleness sweep, device sync, observation dispatch), gas (Blackline poller) and weather (observation evaluate/dispatch) all run inside the same host. Ingestion for weather is NOT in this service: it is the separate sensors-service, which the backend reads (read-only DB context + status API).
platform.one_permission_scope: One permission CATEGORY for all three products: weatherstation (category 23): weatherstation:view for every read and weatherstation:edit (or project_builder:manage) for ordinary writes, on Weather Station, Lightning and Gas alike. There is no lightningsensor:* or gasdetector:* permission in the backend (stale comments in the repo still claim otherwise). Three narrower grants in the same weatherstation: family gate the Settings area (the two manage-* grants arrived 2026-09-21): weatherstation:settingsProducts (Connected Products), weatherstation:manage-weather-settings, weatherstation:manage-lightning-settings (the lightning radii/binding write no longer accepts weatherstation:edit). So 'single scope' is accurate for viewing and ordinary editing, not for every settings write.
platform.entitlement: Table project_product: one row per project with three booleans (WeatherStationActive, GasDetectorActive, LightningSensorActive); a project with no row reads all false. GET /api/project/{id}/ProjectProduct needs weatherstation:settingsProducts OR project_builder:manage OR weatherstation:view; PUT (full replace) needs weatherstation:settingsProducts OR project_builder:manage. The Connected Products settings page (Settings > Connected Products) is guarded by the same pair in the front end. The front end reads the flags: a product row is drawn in the rail only when its flag is true, each product route answers Not Found when not entitled, and the base URL lands on the first entitled product (Weather Station, Gas, Lightning) else Settings. The backend product routes do NOT consult project_product (no reference outside the ProjectProduct service/controller), so entitlement is a front-end product switch today, not a server-side access check.

claims.claim: Decoding: the sensors-service decodes the Wirepas protobuf packet, then walks the payload TLV; tag 0x01 with length 32 is the weather station (16 two-byte values, scaled: wind speed/rain/temperature/cumulative rain/pressure/humidity x0.1, PM and TSP and CO2 and wind direction x1, H2S/SO2/CO x0.001); 0x7FFF means the sensor is not connected and is stored as empty.
claims.safe_phrase: Each station reading is decoded into plain measurements - wind, rain, temperature, pressure, humidity, dust and gases - and a missing sensor is shown as missing, never as zero.
claims.caveats: The backend ALSO treats 32766 as a second 'not connected' sentinel seen from some firmware (display path rolls back to the previous genuine reading).

claims.claim: Normalising and storing: each packet is matched to a node (node-service registry via foreign data wrapper) to get the project; unmatched packets are dropped with an error; readings are inserted-or-ignored into a TimescaleDB hypertable (1-week chunks); a per-station latest-reading summary row is updated only for live (non-buffered) packets; the reading time is receive time minus travel time.

umbrella_layers: Devices and vendor clouds: weather station, lightning warning unit, portable gas detectors (via the manufacturer's cloud)

Cloud intake: AWS IoT, queues and dead-letter queues (lightning), sensors-service and time-series store (weather), scheduled poll of the vendor cloud (gas)
One WakeCap backend: Weather Station, Lightning Sensor and Gas Detector products in one service, one permission family, per-project product switches
One portal area: Connected Environment menu with Weather Station, Gas, Lightning, Reports and Settings; wallboard and phone views

Gas detector -> manufacturer's cloud (black box) <- WakeCap signs in and polls on a timer; optional push messages are only acknowledged -> neutral gas store -> alerts and site state -> portal, polled about once a minute; acknowledgements stay in WakeCap
